recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work—not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

rec37BEg2t0vMAbr6.Bio: Michael Martin produces electronic music under the stage name MioWnize (pronounced "My Own Eyes"); from Springfield, MO, he appeared on InnerVerse to discuss perception, music, and the cosmos, sharing a mix of his work.
rec37BEg2t0vMAbr6.Name: Michael Martin (MioWnize)

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Talent as a function of caring", "body": "Chance opens with the idea that shaped InnerVerse from the start: the gap between people and their heroes is time and effort, and what gets called talent is really a measure of how much you care. He adds a second layer he learned along the way, that your capacity to care about your passions tracks how well you care for yourself. Later he puts that to Michael directly, and Michael says that since leaving Springfield, unplugging from the internet and focusing on the farm, his music and his hopes for a career in music have started to take shape."}, {"title": "Off the grid on a Missouri family farm", "body": "Michael now lives on his fiancée's family farm near Troy in Lincoln County, where he gets decent hotspot data for about a week a month, uploads everything to SoundCloud in that window, then disappears into Ableton. His old studio was a closet facing a neighbor's house; now his window looks over a bluff down to the Cuivre River, with eagles flying past. He has taken up foraging chicken of the woods and lion's mane, and Chance links this rhythm to what he describes as natural monthly creative ebbs and inward phases that a Monday to Friday schedule ignores."}, {"title": "Dense but intelligible electronic music", "body": "Michael describes rooting a track in one groove or chord pattern and fleshing out every fractal direction it can go within two to four minutes, sometimes stacking around 150 channels and then cleaning up the mud so each sound gets its own space. The conversation borrows a sculpture metaphor, where less material ends up saying more. Chance says Michael plays the digital world like a virtuoso guitarist, with a soulful humanness he finds rare in cookie cutter electronic music, while Michael insists there is no shame in simplicity, since much of the music he loves is crazy simple."}, {"title": "New tracks, trumpet and the Undone EP", "body": "After some live troubleshooting, the stream plays two MioWnize tracks from SoundCloud. First Impressions is headed for an EP called Undone, which Michael says includes some of his own processed singing, and he reveals the trumpet on it is really him, picking back up the instrument he played in middle and high school. The second track starts chill before twisting into something spacey and in your face. Michael also talks about a new studio job where he is about to record a metal band, a hoped for set at Dancefestopia, and a farm retreat idea Chance dubs a music bed and breakfast."}, {"title": "Screens, faces and a disconnected culture", "body": "Paul, a listener who joins the stream from Lexington, Kentucky, brings observations from years of grocery work: supply chains he expects to strain further, and a growing share of young children who ignore Trader Joe's stickers because they are hunched over phones. The group talks about why seeing human faces matters and how masks turn regular customers into strangers. Michael argues that people slip into a conditioned perception of the reality they manifest, a loop that is hard to break, and says outlets like Chance's show can help pull people out to see for themselves."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Michael Martin makes magical music under the moniker MioWnize. Join us to spread some positive vibes on your life sandwich.
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "Even aptitude, or the myth of talent, is more of a function of how much you care than something innately within you.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "When I intend for others to hear my music, I want them to see through my own eyes.", "author": "Michael Martin (MioWnize)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b3b2a861-5885-4756-8040-c998150ef6e7/MICHAEL-MARTIN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Just having my studio with a window facing a bluff down to the Cuivre River, and I can just see eagles fly over out of this window.", "author": "Michael Martin (MioWnize)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b3b2a861-5885-4756-8040-c998150ef6e7/MICHAEL-MARTIN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "We have a creative ebb, and then a sort of recession of our energy more into an introspective, inward state, and we're naturally supposed to have that.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "In my head you can come up with the most elaborate stuff, but actually getting it out, especially when you're sitting in a session, is almost impossible.", "author": "Michael Martin (MioWnize)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b3b2a861-5885-4756-8040-c998150ef6e7/MICHAEL-MARTIN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I feel like you play the digital world the way that a virtuoso guitar player does. It doesn't feel unoriginal, and it doesn't even feel unorganic, even though it's electronic.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "What I do is I kind of just flesh out every single different fractal direction that that groove can possibly go.", "author": "Michael Martin (MioWnize)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b3b2a861-5885-4756-8040-c998150ef6e7/MICHAEL-MARTIN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "There's no shame to simplicity in music. A lot of the coolest music that I enjoy is so crazy simple to me that I couldn't even think of myself making it.", "author": "Michael Martin (MioWnize)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b3b2a861-5885-4756-8040-c998150ef6e7/MICHAEL-MARTIN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Maybe you just need to open up a suite, like a bed and breakfast. Let someone rent out a room in your house, and then you also take them over to the studio and help them record a track. It'll be like music bed and breakfast.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I feel people kind of get into this conditioned perception of what they manifest their reality to be.", "author": "Michael Martin (MioWnize)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b3b2a861-5885-4756-8040-c998150ef6e7/MICHAEL-MARTIN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
